calls.reason: No direct OpenAI or Anthropic debt issue with a known yield was found. The only sub-8% figure is preliminary June pricing for a Broadcom-backed chip vehicle, not either lab's own issue.
Oracle's own call says 75% of Abilene is delivered, and nothing independent measures installed capacity. Only Wisconsin shows a documented delay risk, so 'every campus heavily behind' is unproven.
Anthropic had only filed its S-1 by October 26 and was not yet public. The claim's condition, and the debt issuance it predicts, have not happened.
The claim assumes a post-IPO setting at a $2 trillion valuation, which had not arrived; OpenAI's disclosed valuation was $852 billion. No twelve-month record of debt raised exists to test it.
Cipher's zero-coupon convertible in October hints at cheap borrowing, but its conversion costs make the true cost unclear. No broad comparison of financing terms was found.
FT reporting says KBRA was given adjusted operating income and had to estimate missing cash-flow figures. That is mixed, and it does not show EBTIT itself was used or ignored.
